newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN seeks funds for Cechnya displaced.
newsitem.headline: UN seeks funds for Cechnya displaced.

text.p: The United Nations appealed on Friday for $11.9 million to feed and care for 75,000 people displaced from Chechnya and to help them return when it is safe to do so.

Some 140,000 people who fled fighting in the separatist region after December 1994 remain in three neighbouring republics, Ingushetia, North Ossetia and Daghestan. U.N. agencies plan to concentrate of the neediest of them.
A ceasefire was signed between Russian forces and Chechen separatists in August 1996, leading to a troop withdrawal.
But the appeal by U.N. agencies said that "troubling breaches of security" continued to plague humanitarian operations in the region and will delay repatriation.
Six staff of the International Committee of the Red Cross were killed last December, leading relief agencies to withdraw.

"As a result, U.N. activities planned in Chechnya under the appeal will not be implemented immediately. The situation will be reviewed in March with the aim of resuming implementation of projects inside Chechnya," the U.N. appeal statement said.
Funds will be used to provide shelter, water and sanitation, basic education and medical supplies for 75,000 of the most vulnerable of the displaced. Cholera persists in the region.
Participating agencies include the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, the U.N. Children's Fund, the World Health Organisation and the Department of Humanitarian Affairs.

UNHCR, which would organise voluntary repatriation, said: "Emphasis will be also placed on the integration of internally displaced persons who will not return to Chechnya and opt to settle permanently in Ingushetia and Daghestan."
Donors funded about 90 percent of a $13 million appeal for Chechnya in 1996.
